name: Revit
tagline: Autodesk's BIM authoring tool for buildings: parametric 3D models that generate drawings, schedules, and coordination data.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Revit is not an app, it is a parametric geometry kernel plus a 30-year accretion of building-industry conventions wrapped in a document engine. The hard part is not drawing walls, it is that a wall knows its layers, hosts a window, trims to a roof, appears correctly in six view types, and reports its area into a schedule that a quantity surveyor will bill from. Even if an agent nailed the modeling, you still cannot hand your file to a structural engineer, a contractor, or a planning authority, because they all expect RVT or a clean IFC export that survives round-tripping. Families, shared parameters, worksharing, and firm-specific templates are years of accumulated setup that no one rebuilds voluntarily. A one-shot build gets you a toy floor plan editor, which is genuinely useful for exactly one person doing exactly one small thing.
coreLoopDIY: A local 2D floor plan sketcher where walls, doors, and windows are objects with parameters, and the drawing auto-generates an area and opening schedule you can export.
requirements: willingness to never share the file with another professional
whatYouLose: Interoperability: no RVT, no reliable IFC, so consultants and contractors cannot open your work
Parametric families and the enormous library of manufacturer content
Automatic drawing production: sections, elevations, callouts, sheets, and dimension updates that propagate from the model
Worksharing and central models, so more than one person on a project is off the table
Structural, MEP, and analysis workflows that make it a coordination tool rather than a drawing tool
moatNotes: The real lock-in is social: your engineers, your fabricator, and your planning submission all assume the same file format and the same template conventions.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the licence is not what you are buying. You are buying the ability to send a model to eleven other firms and have it open, to hire someone who already knows the software, to pull a schedule that a cost consultant trusts, and to produce a drawing set that a building authority accepts. For a firm, one coordination failure costs more than a year of seats, so the price is barely discussed. For an architecture student or a hobbyist doing a house extension, it is wildly disproportionate, which is why SketchUp, Archicad trials, and free IFC viewers exist in that gap.
notes: A parametric wall is a weekend build; a building model that eleven other firms can open is not. The moat is file-format gravity plus every consultant, contractor, and planning office that already assumes it.
prompt:
Build a local-first 2D floor plan sketcher with parameter-aware building elements. This is a personal tool, not a BIM replacement.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + TypeScript, no framework beyond vanilla DOM
- Canvas 2D for the drawing surface
- Zustand-free: one plain state module with undo/redo via a command stack
- Persist to IndexedDB via idb-keyval, plus JSON import/export
- No accounts, no server, no telemetry, no cloud. Runs with npm run dev and nothing else.

In scope:
- Draw walls by clicking points on a snapping grid (configurable, default 100mm). Walls are objects with: type name, thickness, height, and an ordered list of material layers with thicknesses.
- Walls join cleanly at corners and T-junctions: compute the mitred outline so the plan reads correctly.
- Place doors and windows as hosted openings: pick a wall, set offset along wall, width, height, sill height. Opening cuts the wall in the drawing and moves with the wall when the wall is edited.
- Detect closed wall loops and create rooms automatically. Each room gets a name, a computed floor area, and a perimeter.
- A schedules panel with three tables: rooms (name, area, perimeter), openings (type, width, height, host wall, room), walls (type, length, area, layer buildup). Export each to CSV.
- A dimension tool: click two points, get a persistent dimension annotation.
- Element type library: define a wall type or door type once, reuse it, edit the type and all instances update.
- Print-to-PDF view at a chosen scale (1:50, 1:100) via a CSS print stylesheet with a scale bar and north arrow.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- 3D, roofs, stairs, structural or MEP
- IFC or DWG or RVT import/export
- Multi-user editing or sync
- Automatic sections and elevations

Ship a README that states plainly: this file cannot be opened by anyone else's software, so do not use it for anything you have to hand over.
